title: Common restricted value of the two coefficient-tower paths
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X^e,\mathcal C_S^e$ be categories [def-nagata-category], for three coefficient labels $e=r,s,t$. Give functors $L^e:\mathcal C_X^e\to\mathcal C_S^e$, $E^e:\mathcal C_S^e\to\mathcal C_X^e$, and natural isomorphisms $\rho^e:L^eE^e\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Products of functors mean functional composition with canonical associators inserted. For each pair $ij=rs,st,rt$ give functors $F_Y^{ij}:\mathcal C_Y^i\to\mathcal C_Y^j$, $Y=X,S$, and natural isomorphisms
$$q^{ij}:L^jF_X^{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_S^{ij}L^i,\qquad h^{ij}:F_X^{ij}E^i\xrightarrow{\sim}E^jF_S^{ij}$$
such that
$$\rho^jF_S^{ij}\circ L^j(h^{ij})=F_S^{ij}(\rho^i)\circ(q^{ij}E^i).\tag{N}$$
Give natural isomorphisms $t_Y:F_Y^{st}F_Y^{rs}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Y^{rt}$ for $Y=X,S$ satisfying
$$q^{rt}\circ(L^t t_X)=(t_SL^r)\circ F_S^{st}(q^{rs})\circ(q^{st}F_X^{rs}).\tag{Q}$$
For $M\in\mathcal C_S^r$ define arrows from $A=F_X^{st}F_X^{rs}E^rM$ to $B=E^tF_S^{rt}M$ by
$$h_L=E^t(t_S(M))\circ h^{st}(F_S^{rs}M)\circ F_X^{st}(h^{rs}(M)),\qquad h_R=h^{rt}(M)\circ t_X(E^rM).$$
Both restricted paths have the following common value, naturally in $M$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho^t(F_S^{rt}M)\circ L^t(h_L)
&=t_S(M)\circ F_S^{st}F_S^{rs}(\rho^r(M))\circ F_S^{st}(q^{rs}(E^rM))\circ q^{st}(F_X^{rs}E^rM)\\
&=\rho^t(F_S^{rt}M)\circ L^t(h_R).
\end{aligned}\tag{L}$$
In particular $L^t(h_L)=L^t(h_R)$. No faithfulness of $L^t$ or equality of the unrestricted paths is asserted.

proof.text:
Fix $M$ and abbreviate $U=E^rM$, $V=F_S^{rs}M$, $W=F_S^{rt}M$, $a=h^{rs}(M)$, $b=h^{st}(V)$, $c=h^{rt}(M)$, $u=t_S(M)$ and $v=t_X(U)$. Set
$$P=\rho^t(W)\circ L^t(h_L),\quad R=\rho^t(W)\circ L^t(h_R),\quad C=u\circ F_S^{st}F_S^{rs}(\rho^r(M))\circ F_S^{st}(q^{rs}(U))\circ q^{st}(F_X^{rs}U).$$
Use the associativity and identity laws of [def-nagata-category] to omit parentheses. A functor preserves identity morphisms and composition; a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ has $G(f)\circ\alpha_A=\alpha_B\circ F(f)$ for $f:A\to B$; an isomorphism has a two-sided inverse. These are the definitions used below, with the components of natural isomorphisms regarded as arrows. All displayed composites have source $L^tF_X^{st}F_X^{rs}U$ and target $W$ when completed to $P,R,C$.

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 1

proof.text:
Expand $h_L$ and use functoriality of $L^t$. Naturality of $\rho^t:L^tE^t\to1$ at $u:F_S^{st}V\to W$ gives
$$\rho^t(W)\circ L^tE^t(u)=u\circ\rho^t(F_S^{st}V).$$
Substitute this identity into the expansion, and then substitute (N) for the pair $st$ at the object $V$:
$$P=u\circ F_S^{st}(\rho^s(V))\circ q^{st}(E^sV)\circ L^tF_X^{st}(a).$$

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 2

proof.text:
The arrow $a:F_X^{rs}U\to E^sV$ belongs to $\mathcal C_X^s$. Apply the defining naturality equation of $q^{st}:L^tF_X^{st}\to F_S^{st}L^s$ to this particular arrow:
$$q^{st}(E^sV)\circ L^tF_X^{st}(a)=F_S^{st}L^s(a)\circ q^{st}(F_X^{rs}U).$$
Substituting into the previous expression and combining adjacent functor images gives
$$P=u\circ F_S^{st}(\rho^s(V)\circ L^s(a))\circ q^{st}(F_X^{rs}U).$$

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 3

proof.text:
Equation (N) for $rs$ evaluated at $M$ is exactly
$$\rho^s(V)\circ L^s(a)=F_S^{rs}(\rho^r(M))\circ q^{rs}(U).$$
Substitute it in the expression from step 3 and distribute $F_S^{st}$ over this composition. The result is $P=C$, including every factor and its order in the first equality of (L).

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 4

proof.text:
Expand $h_R=c\circ v$ and apply (N) for $rt$ at $M$. This gives
$$R=F_S^{rt}(\rho^r(M))\circ q^{rt}(U)\circ L^t(v).$$
Equation (Q) evaluated at $U$ replaces its last two factors, so
$$R=F_S^{rt}(\rho^r(M))\circ t_S(L^rU)\circ F_S^{st}(q^{rs}(U))\circ q^{st}(F_X^{rs}U).$$

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 5

proof.text:
The arrow $\rho^r(M):L^rU\to M$ belongs to $\mathcal C_S^r$. The defining naturality equation of $t_S:F_S^{st}F_S^{rs}\to F_S^{rt}$ at this arrow is
$$F_S^{rt}(\rho^r(M))\circ t_S(L^rU)=t_S(M)\circ F_S^{st}F_S^{rs}(\rho^r(M)).$$
Substituting in step 5 gives $R=C$. Together with step 4 this is the two equalities in (L). Compose $P=R$ on the left with the specified inverse of $\rho^t(W)$; associativity and its inverse identity give $L^t(h_L)=L^t(h_R)$.

source.place: (3), final compatibility sentence; agent-written component calculation, step 6

proof.text:
The equality is natural in $M$. Here is the elementary verification needed for the composites: for $\alpha:F\to G$, $\beta:G\to H$ and $f:M\to N$,
$$H(f)\circ\beta_M\circ\alpha_M=\beta_N\circ G(f)\circ\alpha_M=\beta_N\circ\alpha_N\circ F(f).$$
Applying a functor to a naturality equation preserves it, by preservation of composition; evaluating a natural transformation after a functor preserves it by substituting that functor's image of $f$. Thus each factor in $P,R,C$ is a whiskered component of one of the given natural isomorphisms, and the displayed two-line calculation proves that each composite is natural. More explicitly, writing $T=F_S^{rt}$ and $D=L^tF_X^{st}F_X^{rs}E^r$, each $J=P,R,C$ satisfies $T(f)\circ J_M=J_N\circ D(f)$. Hence the component equalities just proved are equalities of natural transformations, as claimed.
